target.title: fix(proxy-capture): honor response backpressure and client abort
target.body:
Closes #105701

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the debug proxy capture server would forward upstream response bodies without honoring `ServerResponse.write()` backpressure, and could crash or leave work running when a client aborted mid-stream. Operators and test fixtures using the debug proxy could see unbounded memory growth under slow clients and unhandled write errors on disconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

The HTTP response forward path uses Node native `Readable.pipe()` for backpressure, keeps body-preview capture as an independent `data` observer, cancels upstream on client abort, and preserves pre-header 502 / post-header abort behavior on upstream errors. Existing partial-upstream-error behavior (complete 502 before headers / abort after headers) is preserved.

## User Impact

Debug proxy traffic capture remains available for local diagnostics and fixture recording, but slow clients no longer force unbounded buffering of upstream response data, and mid-response client aborts no longer leave the proxy in a fragile write-after-end state. No product config or user-facing channel behavior changes.

## Evidence

**Verification host:** local macOS (agent; CS option 1 follow-up)

Commands run after native-pipe refactor:

```text
pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.ts src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts
# pass

pnpm exec oxlint src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.ts src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts
# 0 warnings / 0 errors

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts
# 9/9 passed

# Real proxy process proof (origin + startDebugProxyServer in-process listeners,
# real HTTP clients over loopback — not unit Fake streams):
# slow client pause-after-first-chunk, mid-response abort, subsequent /healthy
```

Focused tests:
- native pipe backpressure + capture observer
- client abort destroys upstream
- mid-response abort + later healthy request through same proxy

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Debug proxy forwards upstream bodies via Node native `Readable.pipe()` backpressure; preview capture is an independent `data` observer; client abort cancels upstream; later requests still succeed.
- Environment: local macOS, branch tip after CS follow-up commit, Node via `pnpm exec tsx` / `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Current-main contrast: main ignored `write()` false (no backpressure). First PR revision used a hand-written pause/drain controller; CS asked for native pipe + real-process proof.
- Exact steps after this patch:
  1. Refactor `pipeUpstreamBodyToClient` to `upstreamRes.pipe(res)` with capture observer + abort cancel.
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts` → 9/9.
  3. Real-process proof: start streaming origin + `startDebugProxyServer` listeners; HTTP client slow-read; abort after first chunk; GET `/healthy` on same proxy.
- Evidence after fix (redacted loopback ports):

```text
[proof] origin listening on 127.0.0.1:65525
[proof] proxy process server listening on http://127.0.0.1:65526
[proof] step1: slow client through real proxy
[proof] slow client: pausing reads for 200ms after first chunk
[proof] step1 done: status=200 chunks=202 bodyBytes=1905 aborted=false
[proof] step2: mid-response client abort
[proof] client abort after first chunk (8 bytes)
[proof] step2 done: aborted=true chunks=1
[proof] step3: subsequent healthy request on same proxy
[proof] step3 done: status=200 body="ok" complete=true
[proof] PASS: real proxy survived slow client + abort and served later request
```

- Control check: unit suite still covers capture + abort destroy; vitest 9/9 green; oxlint/oxfmt clean on touched files.
- Observed result: slow client completed; abort cancelled mid-stream; subsequent healthy returned 200 `ok` on the same proxy.
- What was not tested: CONNECT tunnel backpressure (still socket pipe), multi-GB responses, non-macOS hosts, full-repo CI.

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Human operator owns the contributor fork push and PR submission policy for this pipeline.
